outputs.L3:
The flexible storage device is intended for packaging, storing, and transporting particulate solid substances or liquids. It is particularly suited for materials that require a flexible container capable of being lifted, handled, and filled or emptied efficiently.

The device comprises a bottom and a plurality of lateral walls that together define a storage volume. Near the upper portion of the device, hanging loops are provided to allow the device to be lifted, moved, or suspended by suitable handling equipment. These loops are positioned close to the top of the container so that the load can be supported in a stable manner during lifting and transport.

The storage volume is formed, at least in part, by a flexible external wrapper. This external wrapper defines at least the four lateral walls of the device and provides the outer structure of the container. Because the wrapper is flexible, the storage device can adapt to the shape and distribution of the material contained inside it while still maintaining an overall packaging configuration.

Inside the external wrapper, the device further includes a flexible tubular internal wrapper. This internal wrapper is secured to the external wrapper and extends vertically within the storage volume. Its arrangement divides the interior of the device into five vertical compartments. These compartments include a central compartment defined by the tubular internal wrapper and four additional compartments arranged around it between the internal wrapper and the lateral walls of the external wrapper.

The tubular internal wrapper therefore forms a central vertical compartment having both an upper mouth and a lower mouth. The upper mouth allows access to the central compartment from above, while the lower mouth provides communication toward the lower region of the storage volume. The upper edge of the internal wrapper is positioned at the same height as, or below, the upper edge of the lateral walls of the external wrapper. This configuration ensures that the internal wrapper remains within the overall height of the storage device while still effectively dividing the storage volume into the desired vertical compartments.
outputs.L4:
A flexible storage device is provided for holding, transporting, and handling particulate solids, granular materials, powders, or liquids. The device includes an external wrapper that defines the outer shape of the storage package and forms the main lateral walls of the container. Within this external wrapper, a tubular internal wrapper is securely attached so that the total storage volume is divided into a plurality of separate compartments.

The internal wrapper extends generally vertically inside the external wrapper and defines a central vertical compartment. Between the internal wrapper and the surrounding external wrapper, the remaining storage space is divided into four peripheral compartments arranged around the central compartment. This arrangement provides a compartmentalized storage structure in which the contents may be distributed between the central compartment and the surrounding peripheral compartments, improving organization, load distribution, and stability during filling, storage, lifting, or transport.

The tubular internal wrapper is fixed relative to the external wrapper to maintain the intended compartment configuration. Its upper edge is located at or below the upper edge of the lateral walls of the external wrapper. As a result, the internal divider does not project above the outer package wall, while still providing a defined separation between the central storage space and the four surrounding storage spaces.

The completed structure forms a flexible, liftable package suitable for bulk materials. The external wrapper provides the principal containment and lifting body, while the secured tubular internal wrapper creates distinct internal zones. Together, these components produce a compartmentalized flexible container having one central vertical compartment and four peripheral compartments, each capable of receiving and retaining material within a defined portion of the overall storage volume.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, yet it is also one of the most important. It is called the definite article because it points to something specific. When we say “a book,” we may mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that the speaker and listener both understand.

This simple word helps make communication clearer. It can identify a person, place, object, or idea: “the teacher,” “the city,” “the answer,” or “the future.” Without it, sentences can sound incomplete or confusing.

“The” also gives importance to what follows it. For example, “the moment” can suggest a special or unforgettable time, while “the truth” can feel powerful and final. In titles, names, and everyday speech, “the” helps shape meaning.

Although it is short and often unnoticed, “the” plays a major role in English. It reminds us that even the smallest words can carry great value.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a flexible intermediate bulk container with an outer bag, lifting loops, and a tubular inner liner dividing the storage volume into one central and four peripheral vertical compartments.
counterfactuals.output: A flexible intermediate bulk container includes an outer bag defining an internal storage volume and having a plurality of lifting loops secured thereto. A tubular inner liner is disposed within the outer bag and is configured to subdivide the internal storage volume into a plurality of vertically extending compartments, including a central compartment and four peripheral compartments arranged about the central compartment. The liner may be formed from flexible sheet material and shaped or joined to define compartment walls that extend between upper and lower regions of the container, thereby restricting lateral migration of bulk material during filling, handling, lifting, and discharge. The compartmentalized liner structure promotes load stability, improved shape retention, and reduced bulging of the outer bag while maintaining the collapsible and flexible characteristics of the intermediate bulk container.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the following invention in one paragraph using formal patent language: a flexible storage bag for powders or liquids, with four side walls, hanging loops, and an internal tubular wrapper attached to the side walls to form five compartments, where the inner wrapper’s top edge does not extend above the outer walls.
counterfactuals.output: A flexible storage bag for containing powdered or liquid materials comprises an outer bag body formed by four side walls defining an internal storage volume and an upper opening, the bag body further including hanging loops secured thereto for supporting and handling the bag. An internal tubular wrapper is disposed within the storage volume and attached to the side walls so as to subdivide the storage volume into five compartments. The tubular wrapper includes an upper edge positioned at or below the upper edges of the side walls, such that the tubular wrapper does not project above the outer bag body.

a flexible outer envelope having a bottom wall and a plurality of outer side walls extending upwardly from the bottom wall to define an outer interior volume, the outer side walls having upper edges defining a top opening of the outer envelope; and

a flexible tubular inner envelope disposed within the outer interior volume, the tubular inner envelope extending vertically and having an upper mouth and a lower mouth, the tubular inner envelope defining an inner storage compartment within the tubular inner envelope,

wherein the tubular inner envelope and the outer envelope together define four additional vertical storage compartments arranged around the tubular inner envelope between an exterior surface of the tubular inner envelope and interior surfaces of the outer side walls,

four lateral walls joined to define an interior storage volume;
